summary: Procurement kickoff focused on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA thresholds, pricing approvals and onboarding steps for Greenfield Insurance. Redwood AE+SE walked through contract posture, security controls (SSO/KMS/audit), and options for Dedicated vs Hosted. Customer asked for specific redlines on data retention, audit log retention and a performance SLA option for dedicated capacity. Action items and timelines agreed.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-01
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood, AE); Diego Alvarez (Redwood, SE); Sara Patel (Greenfield, Head of Procurement); Ethan Ross (Greenfield, CISO); Priya Menon (Greenfield, VP Eng); Marcus Liu (Greenfield, Legal)

Topics covered: MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs, pricing/commits, onboarding steps, SSO/KMS, audit logs

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Sara (Greenfield): Yep, loud and clear, thanks.
[00:12] Maya: Cool, quick intros from our side: I'm Maya Chen, AE, and Diego Alvarez is our SE who will run the technical bits.
[00:19] Diego (Redwood): Hi all, hi.
[00:23] Sara: Sara here, head of procurement at Greenfield, joined by Ethan, Marcus, and Priya.
[00:28] Ethan: Morning.

[02:10] Maya: The agenda is procurement/legal — MSA and DPA redlines — SLAs and pricing approvals — and next steps for onboarding. I'll kick with contract posture then hand to Diego for the SSO/KMS and architecture.
[02:30] Priya (Greenfield): Good. We have a bit of a compressed timeline; procurement wants vendor approved by mid-June if possible.
[02:40] Maya: Understood, we can aim for that.

[05:00] Marcus (Legal): We sent a first-pass of the MSA redlines last night. Main concerns: data retention windows in the DPA, indemnities, and audit rights.
[05:12] Maya: Ok noted. On the DPA we typically propose 90 days for non-production logs retention but can discuss longer retain windows for audit artifacts; for PII we have options: hosted API with token-level masking and option for Private deployment where data never leaves your VPC.
[05:35] Ethan: Important to clarify encryption in transit and at rest, and whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys / HSM.
[05:42] Diego: Yes — we support KMS integrations and an HSM-backed option for Private deployments; for hosted we have envelope encryption with provider KMS and offer Bring-Your-Own-Key for Enterprise plans.

[08:20] Sara: From procurement: pricing — we need committed capacity numbers and a pricing spreadsheet to route through finance. Also what the SLA tiers look like.
[08:35] Maya: We'll send a provisional pricing sheet after this call; baseline hosted API pricing and reserved/dedicated tiers with monthly commit discounts. We can include a sample commitment for 3-month and 12-month terms.
[08:50] Marcus: On SLAs — we need uptime SLA and an latency SLO tied to the model variant; do you commit to tail latency at 95th percentile?
[09:05] Diego: We typically provide uptime SLAs for Dedicated and Hosted; for latency we provide target SLOs (p95) per model/hardware profile — for example our smallest dedicated config aims for p95 < 150ms for short prompts on quantized models, but we should run a quick benchmark with your payload to confirm.

[12:00] Priya: We have two main workloads: customer support triage (low latency) and batch claims processing (throughput). We'll need guidance on which models and dedicated sizing to choose.
[12:18] Diego: Got it — we can propose a split: small dedicated pool for low-latency inferencing and a separate batch pool that optimizes for throughput and cost. Batching/kv cache configs reduce unit cost for batch jobs.

[15:30] Sara: Back to the DPA: retention for logs — Marcus wants at least 1 year of audit log retention for compliance, but for raw transcripts containing PII we want deletion after 90 days unless flagged.
[15:45] Marcus: Right. Also we want a clause that says Redwood won't use our data for model training.
[15:53] Maya: We can confirm in writing — hosted plans can include a clause that customer data is not used for training; Private deployments of course keep everything in your environment.

[18:40] Ethan: For SSO we use SAML 2.0 and will need role mapping into RBAC. Also MFA enforced. How is onboarding for SAML typically handled?
[18:52] Diego: We have a standard SAML connector and support role mapping. Diego: we'll provide the SAML metadata and a sample attribute mapping. Setup is usually 1-2 business days if you have IdP team available.
[19:10] Priya: Any gotchas around VPC peering or firewall rules?
[19:17] Diego: For Private deployments we coordinate with your network team; for hosted we can do VPC egress allow-listing and private endpoints. We'll share a network requirements doc.

[22:00] Maya: Pricing question from finance — is there an overage policy for committed capacity?
[22:10] Maya: Our committed plans include a burst bucket; overages billed at a higher per-token rate. We'll put exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[22:20] Sara: Can you provide example invoices or T&Cs for billing frequency and tax treatment?
[22:27] Maya: Yes we'll include sample invoices.

[25:00] Marcus: Liability caps — default Redwood MSA proposes a liability cap equal to fees paid in the prior 12 months; we may need negotiation to align with our risk matrix.
[25:12] Maya: I'm happy to flag that with legal — we can discuss options for higher caps with enterprise terms.

[28:30] Diego: Technical note — for your batch claims flow with long contexts we recommend a model variant with longer kv cache tuning; we'll provide a quantization suggestion to reduce GPU costs while maintaining accuracy.
[28:45] Priya: Would quantization affect our hallucination rates on domain-specific prompts?
[28:52] Diego: Slightly possible — we'll include eval results on a representative prompt set during the pilot.

[32:00] Sara: Timeline — procurement needs approval by June 15; legal wants to close redlines by June 10. Is that feasible?
[32:12] Maya: Feasible if we get your redline doc back today and Marcus can confirm priority items. We'll target a redline reply by June 4 from our side.
[32:22] Marcus: Ok we'll mark critical items: data retention, training-use prohibition, auditable logs and liability cap.

[35:00] Maya: We'll also propose a pilot: two-week trial with a small dedicated pool to validate latency and throughput. Pricing can be credited toward committed capacity if you expand.
[35:12] Priya: That sounds right — our engineering team wants measurable p95 and throughput numbers from the pilot.
[35:20] Diego: We'll configure latency and throughput dashboards and share tracing hooks.

[38:40] Ethan: Auditability — do you provide immutable audit logs and export in JSON/CSV?
[38:50] Diego: Yes we expose audit logs with retention policies and can provide a secure S3 export or streaming to your SIEM.
[38:58] Ethan: Great. Also need SOC2 type II and ISO docs.
[39:05] Maya: We'll share our security pack and SOC2 report as part of the post-call artifacts.

[42:00] Sara: On the DPA, we might want a clause on subcontractors and data flow. How does Redwood handle third-party processors?
[42:12] Maya: We list subprocessors in the DPA; for Private deployments there's minimal exposure. For hosted we can provide a subprocessors list and commit to notify you on changes.

[45:00] Marcus: A few drafting notes: please send the MSA w/ tracked changes and a companion redline summary called out by section. That helps speed review.
[45:12] Maya: Absolutely — we'll do a redline summary and mark high-priority asks.

[47:30] Priya: Onboarding tasks — what's the expected lead time for Private vs Dedicated?
[47:40] Diego: Dedicated reserved capacity typically takes 2-4 weeks for provisioning depending on region and hardware availability; Private (VPC) onboarding often 2-6 weeks depending on network approvals. We'll give a timeline matrix.

[50:10] Maya: Ok quick recap — action items, we will: send redline-ready MSA/DPA and pricing spreadsheet, share SLAs and SSO/KMS docs, schedule the technical deep-dive, and propose a pilot for dedicated capacity.
[50:25] Sara: Thanks, that works.
[50:30] Marcus: We'll consolidate our redlines and prioritize critical asks, aiming to get them back by EOD tomorrow.
[50:40] Maya: Great — Diego and I will follow up with artifacts. Thanks everyone.
[50:50] Diego: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
